title: DIY calf raise to train calves at home
summary: Tutorial for an improvised seated calf raise: sit on a bench with a barbell (ideally an EZ bar) across the knees and feet on a block or stacked plates for full range of motion. It can't be loaded very heavy, but he thinks calves grow better with volume and frequency, and it avoids the knee pain machines give him.

claims.claim: You can build a seated calf raise at home with just a barbell (an EZ bar is more comfortable), a bench and a block or stack of plates.
Put the feet on a block or plates high enough that the heels don't touch the floor, to get full range of motion and a full stretch.
This setup is harder to load heavily, but calves usually aren't trained that heavy anyway.
He believes calves grow better with volume and frequency than with heavy loads.
Modern calf-raise machines give him bad knee pain and tendinitis because the pad sits directly on top of the knee joint; with a barbell you can place the load where it feels comfortable.
If the bar position stresses the knees, slide it back up the thighs and compensate with more reps.
An EZ bar's crease sits well even on big legs; a straight bar is less comfortable and less stable because it tends to roll down the legs.

exercises.name: DIY seated calf raise (bench + barbell + block)
cues: feet on a block, heels free for full stretch
move the bar back if knees hurt, do more reps
exercises.why: home-gym calf work that spares the knees
